catalog_quote: Emai is a minor language in the Edoid group (Elugbe 1989). It is spoken in over 10 villages with approximately 20-25,000 speakers. A tonal language, Emai shows lexical and grammatical tones high (ˊ), low (ˋ), and downstep high (ˊ'). Its morphological template for the basic verb is X-stem-Y. X identifies a persistive qualifier prefix and Y encompasses contrasting perfective/ imperfective toneme suffixes. Tones from these suffixes spread onto lexically toneless verbs. The imperfective suffix is a floating low tone. Traces of perfective suffix -í and its high tone are evident in simple clauses with an intransitive verb or a monotransitive verb whose direct object has left dislocated. ... [p. 262] Orthographic conventions reflect those in Schaefer and Egbokhare (1999; 2007; 2017), where o represents a half open back vowel, e a half open front vowel, and vb a voiced bilabial approximant. For tone, acute accent marks high, grave accent signals low, and acute accent followed by an apostrophe designates high downstep.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.quote: Emai is a recently documented Edoid language of south central Nigeria that falls within West Benue Congo in the Niger Congo phylum (Elugbe 1973, Elugbe 1989, Williamson and Blench 2000). It employs lexical and grammatical tone in the context of a relatively rigid SVO word order type (Schaefer and Egbokhare 2007, Schaefer and Egbokbhare 2017). [...] Emai executes a {H} (high) overlay pattern in contrast to the {L} overlay of Dogon. An adnominal controller in Emai prompts a {H} tone overlay onto the lexical tone melody of a (left-adjacent) target. [...] Regardless of pre-overlay lexical tone on these head nouns, their post-overlay tone is {HH}.

tone_statements.quote: Emai is a terraced level tone language with two basic tones, high (H) and low (L). These tones contrast as shown in the examples below: 1 a) ɔ̀kpá 'one' b) ɔ̀kpà 'cock' c) òí 'pomade' d) óì 'thief' ... Emai exhibits downstep (both automatic and non-automatic) in both lexical items and in constructions - affecting both high and low tones. ... At the systematic phonetic level Emai has the following tones: high, low, downstep high, downstep low, downglide, rising and falling tones.
tone_statements.summary: Two basic level tones H, L with terracing; downstepped H and L; falling/rising contours derived by glide formation/elision (6.1.4); elided L floats; tense/aspect marked by tonal melodies.
